fields.subject: Resilient Command Execution
fields.where: the connection's CircuitBreakerFailureCount is left unconfigured (null) or is explicitly configured to 1 or more; the nullable comparison CircuitBreakerFailureCount < 1 that decides whether to skip the circuit breaker evaluates false both when the setting is unset and when it is >= 1, so only an explicit value below 1 disables it
fields.trigger: consecutive execution failures on that connection reach the configured circuit-breaker failure count. The circuit breaker is built with Policy.Handle<Exception>() and wraps the retry policy, so an execution counts as a failure when any exception of any type escapes the retry policy: a non-transient or non-DbException exception that the retry policy does not handle counts immediately, and a transient DbException counts once its retries are exhausted. The breaker does not apply the retry policy's transient-DbException filter.
fields.response: open the circuit so that further executions on that connection fail immediately, without attempting the command, for the connection's configured circuit-breaker test interval — the fail-fast behavior this component's own committed responsibility (components/resilient-command-execution) specifies for a circuit breaker whose consecutive-failure threshold has been reached.
